newsitem.title: FRANCE: Bulgaria bought 120,000 T Argentine wheat - traders.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria bought 120,000 T Argentine wheat - traders.

text.p: Bulgaria has bought 120,000 tonnes of Argentine soft wheat at $168.75 per tonne cost and freight, European grain traders said on Monday.
The wheat is for shipment as of December, they said
The finalisation of the deal made at the end of last week remains subject to the signing of state credit guarantees, they said.
"With Bulgaria, contracts get signed and then cancelled, As long as there is no letter of credit, we must be remain cautious," one trader said.
Last week Bulgaria said that it expected to call a grain tender for 300,000 tonnes of wheat within a week.
On November 21 Bulgaria bought 300,000 tonnes of Argentine wheat for between $133 and $135 fob, for January/March shipment.
Bulgaria, which faces a shortage of grain after excessive exports last year and a poor harvest this summer, has said it may import 1.55 million tonnes of grain in 1996/97.
It has applied to key grain exporters, including some European Union countries, for export credit lines, banking sources said.
France recently turned down a request by Bulgaria for a Coface credit gurantee to import French grain.
The decision was linked to Bulgaria's fragile financial and economic situation.

Until now Bulgaria has been buying some of its wheat from Argentina. Argentine wheat is cheaper than U.S. or European wheat on world markets but Argentina does not grant export credits so traders said it remained unclear how Bulgaria would finance its recent purchases. --Paris newsroom +331 4221 5432
